uncited: This configuration defines the parameters and logic for generating rays and querying the neural radiance field during training and inference.
It solves the problem of balancing rendering fidelity with computational cost by controlling sample density, noise injection, and multi-resolution strategies.

It differs from sibling configurations by focusing specifically on the ray-sampling mechanics and the structure of the rendering kwargs dictionary, rather than initialization weights, architecture, or regularization terms.
The core mechanism involves constructing a `render_kwargs` dictionary that is passed to the volumetric rendering function.
This dictionary controls how rays are discretized into samples and how the network outputs are processed.
- **Ray Discretization**: Rays are sampled at discrete points along their length.
The number of samples ($N_{samples}$) and the distribution (linear vs. inverse depth) determine the spatial resolution of the query.
The configuration of sampling and rendering pipelines is fundamental to Neural Radiance Fields (NeRF) and its variants.
